# GitHub Copilot Instructions for Students

This repository is configured to work with GitHub Copilot for Students.

## About GitHub Copilot for Students

GitHub Copilot is available for free to verified students through the GitHub Student Developer Pack. This AI-powered coding assistant helps you:

- Write code faster with intelligent code completions
- Learn new programming languages and frameworks
- Understand complex code with natural language explanations
- Generate unit tests and documentation
- Debug and fix issues more efficiently

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

1. **Verify your student status**: 
   - Sign up for the [GitHub Student Developer Pack](https://education.github.com/pack)
   - Verify your student status with your school email or documentation

2. **Install GitHub Copilot**:
   - For VS Code: Install the [GitHub Copilot extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=GitHub.copilot)
   - For other IDEs: Visit [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot) for supported editors

### How to Use Copilot

1. **Code Suggestions**: Start typing and Copilot will suggest code completions
2. **Comment-to-Code**: Write a comment describing what you want, and Copilot will suggest implementations
3. **Copilot Chat**: Ask questions about the code directly in your editor
4. **Learn and Improve**: Use Copilot suggestions to learn best practices and patterns

## Best Practices

- Review all Copilot suggestions before accepting
- Use descriptive comments to get better suggestions
- Test all generated code thoroughly
- Learn from the suggestions to improve your coding skills
- Don't rely solely on Copilot - understand the code you're using

## Project Context

This is the Bragboard project (Project-2). When working with Copilot:
- Focus on writing clean, maintainable code
- Follow existing code patterns in the repository
- Add comments to help Copilot understand the project context
- Use Copilot to help write tests for your features

## Support

If you encounter issues with GitHub Copilot:
1. Check your GitHub Student Developer Pack status
2. Verify your IDE extension is up to date
3. Visit [GitHub Support](https://support.github.com/) for help
